postTitle: Growing Your Income: Negotiation and Career Capital
topic: A higher starting salary compounds through every percentage raise

assumptions.notes: Two salaries start at €55,000 and €50,000 and both rise 3% a year for 30 years (year 1 = starting salary). Gap in year t = 5,000 x 1.03^(t-1). Cumulative gap = 5,000 x (1.03^30 - 1) / 0.03 = €237,877, shown as about €238,000. End salaries €129,614 and €117,831. Before tax and inflation; no promotions or job changes. Illustrative.

caption.instagram:
What if one negotiation started you €5,000 higher? Same raises, for thirty years.

Two people start the same job, one at €50,000 and one at €55,000. Both get 3% raises every year. Because each raise is a percentage, the €5,000 gap grows: about €7,600 a year apart by year 15, and about €238,000 of extra salary over 30 years, before tax.

It assumes no promotions, no job changes and a raise every year. Real careers vary, and asking does not always move an offer.
